SCARRED BUT NOT FOR LIFE - THE KIM MCCUSKER STORY

By: Joy Summers | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
When Kim Mckusker was dragged under a taxi for 780 metres at speed, no one thought she would live. Six years later she documents her road to recovery and how she survived

Unique Selling Point:
`dramatic narrative from an intelligent and attractive woman

Summary:
Six years ago Kim Mckusker and her fiancé were on their way to gym in the early morning traffic. A taxi pushed past them on the Lonehill road and bumped their vehicle. What happened next soon hit the early morning airwaves. Kim had been dragged under a TAXI for 780 metres. But this was no accident. Instead news reported the story as a road range incident. Now 6 years later Kim tells what really happened on that dreadful morning that would change her life forever. And she documents the painful road to recovery back from near death to life.


Further information:
As he hit me and I went down and under the taxi, which was now speeding up, my instinct kicked in. I told myself to keep my head and neck as far away from the road as I could under the circumstances. I knew I was in trouble the minute the driver had looked at me. I knew this was no accident. And now I knew I was in for a serious ride. What I did not know, until then, was that a person could so viciously and deliberately harm another human being, a complete stranger. Perhaps I was naïve and perhaps my fortunate life had shown me differently, but to experience such malice first hand was beyond shocking to me.
I didn’t experience the stereotypical “life flashing before my eyes” or being summoned “into the light” as many people apparently do in near-death experiences. I didn’t experience anything close to either of those. This isn’t to say I don’t believe some people have these experiences in near-death situations, but perhaps this only happens if you think you’re going to die. In my mind, in that moment, I only thought of two things and neither of them was about ending up dead. One – keep your head up. Two – this is bad, but this man is still human; he will stop soon. On thought one, I was “in control” and could make this happen to a certain extent. On thought two, I couldn’t have been more wrong.
As the taxi driver accelerated and with me already stuck and trapped under the vehicle, somehow – although I can’t tell you exactly how – I managed to hook my forearms into whichever parts I could and I pulled my head and chest towards them. I remember hanging on, literally, for dear life and thinking, no matter what happens, I’m not going to end up brain-damaged. Not even a little. Despite my resolve to keep my head up and off the road, it was impossible to do this successfully as the taxi continued to pick up speed. After the four-way stop I knew that the road opened up and cars routinely picked up speed there. The taxi did just that. With no obstruction in front of him, the driver accelerated – aggressively – and the taxi went faster and faster. Even if I had been able to hold myself up in spite of how fast the taxi was going, I would have required Herculean strength to do so over the distance he would travel.

Press Release:


Scarred, But Not For Life
Almost six years ago a routine early morning drive to the gym changed the life of Kim McCusker in an instant. After a
minor bumper bashing, the taxi driver responsible, refused to give his details to her fiancé. Hoping to assist, Kim
approached the taxi, but she never got to his window, because he accelerated, knocked her over, and seconds later
she was dragged for 780 metres under the vehicle. Carte Blanche tells the remarkable story of her recovery, her will
to live, and her family’s love and support that made it all possible

Script:


Scarred for Life FINAL SCRIPT TX 19th March 2017

Commentary One
In 2011 Kim McCusker became known as the girl who was dragged by a taxi

Derek Link
It was early on a September morning, Kim and her fiancé Lourens, were on their way to gym when right here, a mere bumper bashing turned into a horror story in a matter of seconds

Commentary Two
A taxi pushed past Lourens Grobbler bakkie and scraped the right hand back bumper. Lourens and the taxi driver pulled over onto the shoulder of the road. Lourens got out, hoping to get his details.

Kim
The taxi driver was totally uncooperative and wouldn’t roll down his window, wouldn’t look at Lourens. I then began walking towards the taxi driver. His vehicle was standing still. My intention was to get to his window and see if he would respond better to me

Derek
And you remember his expression even?
Kim
I remember him looking at me walking that entire distance with this look of…. I can only describe it as malice.

Commentary Three
Then unexpectedly the taxi driver accelerated and bumped her, almost to the ground

Kim
And I started screaming you can’t go and at that point he looked at me again, straight through his windscreen with this look of hatred, and went for me.

Commentary Four
Kim relived her experience with me on the actual route

Kim
As he hit me I remember thinking one thing, and that was to keep my head and neck as far away from the tar as possible. I didn’t see my life flash before my eyes. I wasn’t summoned into the light or anything like that

Derek
How were you holding on?
Kim
I managed to hook my forearms into some part of the taxi and pull my upper body away from the ground as much as I could


Derek
It’s just so hard to imagine being dragged this distance
Derek
And here were the security guards on the right- hand side?
Kim/ Derek
And over here eventually brought to a halt with the wheel on your pelvis

LINK
Kim was rushed to this hospital with her life literally hanging in the balance – it took 7 hours just to stabilize her and another 7 hours to clean her wounds with very specialized surgical equipment

Commentary Five
Kim’s mom, Pat McCusker is a nurse, and was on her way to work, when she got the news. She first went to hospital, tended to her own patients, and then made her way to the Life Fourways hospital where she walked straight into the theatre

PAT
I think the thought crossed my mind that I would rather be in that position than see my daughter like that. I would rather have been the one dragged under the taxi if I could have changed things.

DEREK
And Pat, with all your experience you have had, how did you feel when you first saw Kim?

PAT
I was absolutely horrified. Her left ear was off, it had been stitched on again and I looked at those injuries, and I thought this can’t be Kimmy, please let her live. I don’t think I have ever seen someone so badly injured

Commentary six
The tissue, skin and ligament damage was only part of the picture. Kim had seven fractured vertebrae, both knees fractured, a fracture in her right hip and baby finger, extensive cranial injuries, and her left ear almost torn off

Derek
Is it possible to describe the pain of 60% of your body being scrubbed, for over seven hours?
Pat
Kim had 58% of her body grazed – a deep graze it’s like a full thickness burn
Derek
I mean she was eroded, the flesh and uhm ligaments were eroded
Pat
Yes, her skin was off on her elbows, her shoulders, her back, her buttocks, so her feet and her legs were dragged on the tar and her fingers and the back of her head, so I can’t imagine the pain she went through
Derek
And you weren’t even seeing all her injuries?
Pat
No, I didn’t see her back. If I had seen her back I might have become hysterical

Commentary Seven
Initially Kim’s body swelled up. She was sedated, covered in bandages, intubated and unable to speak. When she awoke she had two questions

KIM
My one question was whether I had suffered brain damage which was obviously a concern for me given my thought when I whas hit. And my other question was if my leg was going to be amputated. The answers to both questions weren’t totally convincing but they were no no brain damage and no you won’t lose your leg.

Derek
And that gave you the power, the will to live?
Kim
It was just ok if either of those two things aren’t happening I will survive!

Commentary eight
But she also had to survive the pain

KIM
I was dragged on my back and because of the bone injuries I was forced to lie on the open injuries on my back and be immobilized on these deep open wounds, so that is where the discomfort came from

Commentary nine
A cocktail of painkillers made things easier

KIM
If they offered me morphine and pethidine I wanted it

Commentary ten
Kim had close to 40 procedures. Twice a week for two months she went into theatre

Kim
They use high pressure hoses & little blades to cut out and wash out all that dirt because if you graft over dirt or decaying flesh, it’s going to become infected

Commentary eleven
Even so, Kim looked forward to going into theatre
Kim
For me going into theatre was my favourite time, because it was a relief from the pain




LINK DEREK
The driver was charged with attempted murder but just shy of six years later, there is still no resolution. There have been postponements, dockets lost, and now the driver has absconded

Commentary Twelve
The driver, Matome Thamage had charged Lourens with assault, saying Lourens had smashed his window and assaulted him first

Kim
That was the version of events that was reported in a lot articles and newspapers. Only when he had accelerated and hit me, and driven off, did Lourens run after him and punch through his window.

Commentary Thirteen
Lourens was eventually acquitted of all charges.

Derek
Did she build up anger to the taxi driver?
Pat
Never! I have more anger towards the taxi driver than Kim does.
Kim
If I am angry or bitter about the fact, my life is affected.
Derek
So you don’t feel absolute hatred

Kim
No no not at all
Derek
Possibly disbelief that someone could do this?
Kim
Disbelief, and I would say pity for the guy that did this

Derek Link
After nearly three months of agony in hospital, Kim couldn’t wait to get back home now that sounds comforting, but in reality, it was just another phase in her long road to recovery.

PAT
She was very weak, she was learning to walk again we got a wheel chair – she was on crutches – she had to go to rehab, and bathing, feeding, the colostomy and dressings

Commentary fourteen
Pat took 3 months leave, to attend to her daughter

KIM
She would force me, these are your exercises, you do the rehab, she is tough like that, she pushed me
Derek
Tougher than the nurses hospital nurses
Kim
Yes, she doesn’t take nonsense you know

Commentary fifteen
When Pat went back to work it was left to Julia her younger sister, who was studying at the time to step in and help

Julia
She is amazing, having gone through the same thing I would not be able to do it with dignity able to forgive as easily as she has
Derek
And still smiling?
Ya, still has her happy go lucky attitude she is probably more determined

Commentary sixteen
Nine months later Kim’s determination paid off. She managed to walk down the aisle and marry Lourens

LINK
Kims experience has been widely publicized, what isn’t so well known is that the same driver knocked over a young boy a few months earlier. Kims dad is a lawyer and he decided to represent the family to try and get a payout from the Road Accident Fund

Commentary Seventeen
Love for the law runs in the family, and a year before the accident Kim qualified as an advocate. But last year, she decided the demands of that profession are too taxing, and instead she opened this beauty salon.

Kim
I decided to open a business. Worlds apart from law, and I am currently investing my time and energy into that

Commentary eighteen
Recently her marriage to Lourens ended, but Kim isn’t looking back.

Derek to Kim
What do you think has given you the strength to thrive in a way to be optimistic about life?
Kim
My family has had to go through a lot/ challenges seem to come up you have to keep fighting
Derek
But Kim, I want to know what the secret is
Kim
I don’t know. You have one life, you have to make the most of it, keep going. You keep fighting




Commentary nineteen
It took four years for Kim’s body to heal. Now she says she is scarred, but not for life.

THE END Duration 9: 56

PROMO ONE

In 2011 Kim McCusker was dragged under a taxi and her life hung in the balance. Now she has written her story called Scarred but not for Life.

PROMO TWO
This week, Kim McCusker who was dragged under a taxi, relives what happened.

Derek
How did you keep yourself up
Kim
I managed to hook my forearms into some part of the taxi and pull my upper body away from the ground as much as I could

PROMO THREE

Commentary
Pat McCusker has been a nurse for forty years. Then one morning she got a call. Her daughter Kim had been dragged under a taxi

PAT
and I looked at those injuries, and I thought this can’t be Kimmy, please let her live. I don’t think I have ever seen someone so badly injured

In my mind, in that moment, I only thought of two things and neither of them was about ending up dead. One – keep your head up. Two – this is bad, but this man is still human; he will stop soon. On thought one, I was “in control” and could make this happen to a certain extent. On thought two, I couldn’t have been more wrong. As the taxi driver accelerated and with me already stuck and trapped under the vehicle, somehow – although I can’t tell you exactly how – I managed to hook my forearms into whichever parts I could and I pulled my head and chest towards them. I remember hanging on, literally, for dear life and thinking, no matter what happens, I’m not going to end up brain-damaged. Not even a little. Despite my resolve to keep my head up and off the road, it was impossible to do this successfully as the taxi continued to pick up speed. After the four-way stop I knew that the road opened up and cars routinely picked up speed there. The taxi did just that. With no obstruction in front of him, the driver accelerated – aggressively – and the taxi went faster and faster. Even if I had been able to hold myself up in spite of how fast the taxi was going, I would have required Herculean strength to do so over the distance he would travel.
